info.description:
Full Postman collection for the Banu (Bano) Laravel API — with sample request bodies AND sample response payloads on every endpoint.

## Setup
1. Import this collection.
2. In **Variables**, set `base_url` (default `http://localhost:8080/api`) and `external_api_key` (matches `WORDPRESS_MISSIONARY_API_KEY` in `.env`).
3. Run **Auth → Login** — the test script auto-saves the token into `{{token}}` and every authenticated request picks it up via Bearer auth.

## Response envelope
All JSON responses follow `{ success: boolean, message: string, data: any }`. Errors add an `errors` field with field-level details (e.g. validation).

## Pagination envelope
Paginated lists wrap items: `data: { items: [...], meta: { current_page, per_page, total, last_page } }`.

## Auth
Most routes use Laravel Sanctum bearer tokens. The External endpoint uses the `X-External-Api-Key` header instead.

## Tip — using the saved examples
Open any request → **Examples** dropdown (top right) to inspect the `200`, `201`, `401`, `403`, `404`, or `422` sample payloads.

request.description: Authenticated. Upserts the supplied key/value pairs into the current user's register-data store. Each entry is keyed by (user_id, key) — an existing key is updated in place, a new key is inserted as a new row. There is no limit on the number of distinct keys a user can store; the example below intentionally uses 10 distinct keys to make that clear. IMPORTANT: each logical field must use its own unique key string — sending the same key again (even for what you think is a different field) will overwrite that field's value instead of adding a new one, since this is an upsert keyed by `key`. Values can be any JSON scalar or structure.
